metadata.description: Omelette's design setup: the outside design plugins it uses, each pinned to a commit that was read and checked.

plugins.name: frontend-design
plugins.description: Anthropic's frontend-design skill: commits to an aesthetic direction and a real type pairing before any code, so the result does not fall back to the average look.

plugins.name: impeccable
plugins.description: Paul Bakaus's Impeccable 4.8.2: commands you run on a narrow target (critique, audit, polish, bolder, quieter, typeset, layout, animate and more), a detector with 62 rules and no model behind it, and a hook that leaves notes after UI edits and never blocks. Its engine binary downloads on first use and is checked against pinned checksums. Keep its live mode off: it can start claude with permissions bypassed.

plugins.name: modern-web-guidance
plugins.description: Google Chrome's guides to what the web platform now does natively (dialogs, styled selects, anchor positioning, view transitions). Measured by its authors at +27 to +34 points on their task suite.

plugins.name: references
plugins.description: Two of Meng To's skills (MIT) for working from references: video-to-superprompt turns a screen recording into a section-by-section build prompt (needs ffmpeg), and audit-reference-originality compares a build with its references for copied text, files, numbers, imagery and motion, each red flag citing both sides, with a read-only inventory script.

plugins.name: emil-design-engineering
plugins.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering skills: animate, review-animations, break-ui (worst-case data), prototype (variants behind a picker), mobile-native. The repo's whole skills folder loads, including a few platform skills (Expo, Swift).

plugins.name: gsap-skills
plugins.description: GreenSock's official GSAP skills (MIT): core, timelines, ScrollTrigger, plugins (SplitText, MorphSVG, Flip, DrawSVG), React, performance. For sites with scroll storytelling or already on GSAP. It recommends GSAP whenever no library is named, so leave it out of projects on Motion. GSAP itself is free under GreenSock's own licence, not open source.

plugins.name: motion-techniques
plugins.description: Eight of Meng To's motion skills (MIT), each one effect rather than a look: masked word reveals, a scroll progress timeline, scroll-scrubbed word reveals and visual sequences, horizontal scroll scenes, progressive blur, a cursor reveal between two images, and a pass that pauses offscreen animation and finds leaks. Each covers reduced motion and cleanup. The download is Meng's whole skills folder, about 135 MB, since these sit in two of its folders.

plugins.name: illustration
plugins.description: Meng To's illustration skills (MIT): 14 styles of hand-written SVG spot illustration (flat, outlined cartoon, bold pop, line interior, ink sketch, halftone, one-line, isometric, vintage emblem and more), each with three example cards, a measured palette, a parts kit and a render-and-lint loop. For empty states, onboarding, error pages and feature spots. One style per product; each keeps its own palette. Kits and lint run on plain Node; rendering needs playwright-core and CHROME_PATH set to Brave.

plugins.name: stageshow
plugins.description: Benji Taylor's Stageshow (MIT): faux product UI, as stills or short animations, built against gold examples and filmed frame by frame to catch one-frame jumps and text that does not fit. For case-study stills and films and product heroes. Filming needs playwright-core in the project and Chrome, or CHROME_PATH set to another Chromium (Brave).

plugins.name: hyperframes
plugins.description: HeyGen's HyperFrames 0.9.30 (Apache-2.0): HTML compositions rendered to MP4, with captions, transitions, local voiceover and website capture. For whole case-study films. Needs git-lfs to install (about 400 MB), Node 22 and FFmpeg. Set HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1; its reverse-any-video and style-sampling skills are paid.
